SECTION 0 — ANALYSIS OVERVIEW
Rambus is mispriced. The market has extrapolated a memory-cycle
de-rating into a company that has become structurally more diversified
in the last six quarters, sits on ~$760M of net cash ($7.0/sh), and

April "memory-squeeze" downgrade. Enter only in tranches.

  this is the RED FLAG: RCDs are pulled down by DRAM cycle.

  margins >40% sustained → base ~20-30%.

SECTION 2 — BUSINESS QUALITY
Business in 3 sentences:
Rambus licenses IP (royalties, ~$84M/qtr) and sells memory-interface
chips (DDR5 RCD/data buffers, MRDIMM, chipset; ~$99M/qtr product) to
server OEMs/datacenter. It monetizes the JEDEC DDR5 content transition
through a ~45% RCD duopoly position with Renesas/Montage. Software +
contract revenue are ramping as memory moves to HBM4/agentic-AI.

Understandability: High (semis expert only in depth; for a generalist,
Medium-High). Moat score:
- Intangible assets (IP/patents): 3
- Switching costs: 2
- Network effects: 2 (JEDEC/ecosystem)
- Cost advantage: 2 (fabless, high-margin royalties)
- Economies of scale: 2
- Regulatory barriers: 1
- Data moat: 1
Total: 13/21 — WIDE MOAT. Direction: WIDENING for product (share
 gains, DDR5 → MRDIMM attach), STABLE for royalties.

Lynch: Fast grower with a huge royalty cash-flow kicker (a product-
hybrid). What Lynch would check: inventory, channel, R&D spending vs
revenue, consistency of product execution. Rambus passes on inventory
($44M vs revenue $708M = 16 DIO, healthy), spends R&D at ~34% of
revenue, and executes on schedule (guidance beats 4/4 recent qtrs).

- Rev growth 3-yr CAGR: FY23-25 3-yr CAGR ~23.9% [Arithmetic]
- Op margin: GAAP 36.8% FY25, upward-trending
- ROIC (GAAP): 230/ [1.18B × (1- tax)] ≈ ~20%+ [Estimate]

Total: 15 + 1 = 16/16-equivalent → EXCELLENT.

SECTION 2.5 — ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
Consistent with v2.0 methodology:
- R&D capitalization (3-yr):
  FY23 R&D ~$154M, FY24 ~$187M, FY25 ~$190M [Estimate]

- SBC treatment: FY25 SBC = $54M — treated fully as expense in our
  FCF model. Adjusted FCF = CF ops 360M − capex 27M − SBC 54M =
  ~$279M FY25 [Estimate].
- Operating leases: $0.025B, capitalised (negligible).
- Owner earnings (Buffett):
  NI 230M + D&A 12M − maintenance capex ~20M − ΔWC (less relevant,
  260M Δ is in cash/STI) = ~$230M + adjacent $40-50M SBC-neutral.
  ≈ $205M approx owner earnings.

SECTION 3 — VALUATION (0.6 × ENGINE 4 + 0.4 × ENGINE 3)
Enterprise archetype: transitioning from "Option-Led/High-Beta (E)" to
"Product-Platform Hybrid (D)". Reason: product revenue now ~50% (vs
<30% two years ago), product gross margin ~40%+, product revenue
compound >20% each of last 3 years, and Q2'26 product revenue $99.2M
> royalties $84.2M for the first time — the transition criteria are
met at 60-80%. Blended engine applied, which is more conservative for
a hybrid market and reflects the uncertainty.

Discount rate derivation [Assumption]:
Risk-free (10Y): 4.75% (retrieved Sept-26, note ~4.7-4.8%)
ERP: 4.7% (historical/standard) [Assumption]
Indicated beta: 1.872 [Aggregator, vendor; not trusted but used]
Adjusted beta average: 1.35 (product-royalty hybrid is lower than the
raw semis beta; use 1.35 as compromise)
Cost of equity = 4.75% + 1.35 × 4.7% = 11.1% [Estimate]
WACC: no debt → 11.1% (approx, use 11%). I use 11% for EV discounting;
midpoint scenario raising to 11.5% in high-rate regime.

Cash-flow architecture used — "Owner FCF":
FCF = OCF − capex − SBC (cash SBC treated as expense) − ΔWC.
For a high-margin, net-cash company, OCF is high quality. I built a
5-year explicit owner-FCF forecast, then terminal.
